record.name: Siting, regional infrastructure and access to compute
record.shortName: Siting, regional infrastructure and access to compute
record.role: Connects location choices to service paths, resources and who can actually use capacity.
record.description: Data-center siting combines electricity readiness, fiber routes, latency, climate, water, staffing and the needs of its users. A project can improve connectivity or electrical infrastructure while remaining under construction. Google’s India hub announcement explicitly links the site with surrounding infrastructure work, while EuroHPC’s gigafactory call describes a public access and procurement mechanism. These are different evidence categories from private installed hardware. Owner, operator and access model are separate attributes. Announced investment does not equal completed equipment, and nearby compute is not automatically available to every local user.

interfaces.name: Workload and regional requirements
interfaces.signal: User locations, resource limits and access needs

interfaces.name: Siting/access decision
interfaces.signal: A bounded choice with evidence-backed tradeoffs

record.tradeoff: Proximity can reduce network delay while a different region may have earlier power availability; access rules and reservations can dominate physical nearness.
record.whyAI: Useful compute capacity depends on admission and data paths, so geographical expansion matters through more than building counts.

sources.title: Google AI Hub construction milestone in India
The EuroHPC Joint Undertaking launches the AI Gigafactories Call

record.scale: Facility phases to region and world; geography schematic
mechanism: Define the users, data paths and service objectives that location must support.
Compare actual electrical, network and cooling readiness for the same time horizon.
Identify physical operators and the mechanism through which users receive compute access.
Model resource and latency tradeoffs with explicitly chosen scenario weights.
Keep construction announcements, funding commitments and operational service evidence separate.
record.misconception: Investment dollars are not operating megawatts, and public access programs do not imply every listed facility is already commissioned.

check.question: Which question distinguishes accessible capacity from physical capacity?
options: How many countries appear in the press release?
Who can obtain an allocation, under what conditions and date?
How large is the site’s sign?
check.explanation: Access depends on reservations, procurement and admission policy beyond the presence of equipment.

science.title: Conditional site score
science.explanation: zi is a normalized scenario metric and wi a declared preference weight; the score is dimensionless.
science.assumptions: A teaching decision aid, not an objective scientific ranking; normalization and uncertain inputs must be visible.

record.learningObjective: Explain siting and access tradeoffs without equating investment, geography and available service.
record.engineeringExample: Synthetic choice: Site A offers lower network delay but opens a year later; Site B opens sooner with a longer path. A batch-training user and an interactive-serving user can reasonably choose differently.
record.evidenceNotes: No jurisdiction-specific legal advice or exhaustive regional census is provided. Public project and procurement statements support dated examples only.
